quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when other vehicles are not nearby, and stay farther back from the vehicle ahead. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles in front of you for clues about the road ahead.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but what matters most is seeing the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not protect your face like a face shield or goggles do.

questions.question: What is a horn useful for on a motorcycle?

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.
Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers might not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not work as well as goggles or a face shield for protection.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to anticipate the best course of action.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to anticipate the best course of action.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the direction you are turning.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger on the road for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before you carry a passenger or extra weight on the road, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the added weight.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: You should check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overusing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger changes how your motorcycle handles. You will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: ______ guarantees that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that another vehicle will enter your path if it can.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, about how many drinks are still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed to estimate remaining alcohol. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Do not ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down before hitting an obstacle. Approach it straight on if possible. Just before contact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Before mounting your motorcycle, perform all of the following checks except:

options.text: Testing both brake controls to ensure the brake light works.
Checking that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and that all lights work properly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should riders do?

options.text: Use only mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Brake hard to let vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead by turning only your head. Press your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Which statement about the front brake is true?

options.text: Use it only for quick stops.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is weaker than the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used properly.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to stay visible.
